name: 36. Bedrock Invoke Route Cache Control + Usage Fields (#5629)
description: Regression for #5629. The Bedrock invoke ingress routes (POST /bedrock/model/{id}/invoke and .../invoke-with-response-stream) accept an Anthropic-native request body and convert it to a Bedrock Converse call via BedrockInvokeRequest.ToBedrockConverseRequest(). convertAnthropicTools() and parseSystemMessages() only copied known fields and silently dropped any cache_control marker on a tool or system block, so Bedrock never received a cachePoint and the full prompt prefix was rebilled as fresh input tokens on every turn with no visible signal (responses stayed correct, only usage/billing was wrong). Separately, invoke-with-response-stream's message_delta never carried input_tokens at all regardless of caching, and the non-streaming /invoke response never surfaced cache_creation_input_tokens/cache_read_input_tokens even once the ingress bug is fixed. Cases 1-2 pin the core fix across two sequential turns against the same prefix (turn 1 must create a cache entry, turn 2 must read from it instead of being rebilled in full - the exact defect reported in the issue). Case 3 pins the streaming usage-emission fix independently and cheaply (no caching required). Case 4 is a regression guard: an ordinary invoke call with no cache_control must keep behaving exactly as before the fix (usage present, no spurious cache fields).

item.name: Bedrock invoke: tool+system cache_control creates a cache entry (Haiku 4.5, turn 1) - #5629

exec: pm.test('invoke request with tool+system cache_control succeeds - #5629', function () {
pm.test('invoke turn 1: cache_control on tool+system creates a Bedrock cache entry (regression for #5629 - was silently dropped, no cache field ever appeared) - #5629', function () {
pm.expect(cacheTokens, 'expected a cache breakpoint to be honored, usage=' + JSON.stringify(usage)).to.be.above(0);
